port_instructions: Faithful (recommended) boot: keep the exe's own main/App2/MainPage code; replace only (a) GetActivationFactory (IAT 0x20B5FC) with a router to host fakes, (b) D3D11CreateDevice (IAT 0x20B1A4) clamp to FL 9_1 + BGRA, (c) the swap-chain presentation path (composition swap chain -> HWND). No code patch of MainPage/InitializeComponent is needed if LoadComponent is a no-op and FindName returns the 4 fake elements.

Fake Application.Start(cb): (1) cb->vtbl[3](cb,NULL) on the UI thread; (2) the App2 ctor has by then called your IApplicationFactory.CreateInstance(outer=App2+8): keep+AddRef outer; (3) QI(outer, IApplicationOverrides 25F99FF7-9347-459A-9FAC-B2D0E11C1A0F) -> p; call p->vtbl[7](p, launchArgs) where launchArgs QI(IActivatedEventArgs).get_PreviousExecutionState (slot 7) returns 0; (4) then run a Win32 message loop until WM_CLOSE, servicing: DispatcherTimer ticks, CoreDispatcher.RunAsync queues, and the events listed in startup_flow.md section 'events the host must raise'; (5) return S_OK so main returns.

Events the host MUST raise after OnLaunched returns (UI thread): (i) FrameworkElement.SizeChanged on the SwapChainPanel (handler = delegate registered through IFrameworkElement slot 47) with SizeChangedEventArgs{NewSize = client area in DIPs}; before raising make get_ActualWidth/Height return the same finite values and ISwapChainPanel.get_CompositionScaleX/Y return non-zero (1.0 or the DPI scale); (ii) DispatcherTimer Tick every 50 ms until Stop(). Optional later: CoreWindow.VisibilityChanged, DisplayInformation Dpi/Orientation/DisplayContentsInvalidated, CompositionScaleChanged, InputPane Showing/Hiding, HardwareButtons.BackPressed.

ThreadPool fake: RunAsync / RunWithPriorityAndOptionsAsync must run the WorkItemHandler on a REAL separate thread (Invoke = vtable slot 3, argument = the IAsyncAction); the IAsyncAction needs IAsyncInfo get_Status (0=Started,2=Canceled,1=Completed) and Cancel. The render loop checks the status every iteration and spins at full speed (Present(0,0)); the init job sets AppMain+0x3C when MinecraftClient::init finishes.

Delegate protocol: every event handler pointer passed to an add_X method is the delegate object base; call handler->vtbl[3](handler, sender, args) (r0,r1,r2); tokens are 64-bit EventRegistrationToken written through the out pointer; handlers run synchronously on the calling thread in this code (they take AppMain's critical_section).

Fakes must be agile/free-threaded: Window.Current, DisplayInformation::GetForCurrentView, CoreWindow, panel getters are called from the UI thread, the render thread (AttachToPanel is UI; Minecraft::update uses DX::DeviceResources::get only) and thread-pool threads (HID lambdas call dispatcher.RunAsync).

Replay option (skip only XAML loader): create DR via 0x1dce2c(out), then AppMain via new(0x40)+0x1d9d14(app,&sp); wait for AppMain+0x3C; then DR::SetSwapChainPanel 0x1dbd40(dr,panel) / SetLogicalSize 0x1dbc80(dr, s0=w, s1=h) / OnWindowSizeChanged 0x1da32c / AttachToPanel 0x1da634 / StartRenderLoop 0x1da8a8. All of these still call Window.Current, CoreWindow, DisplayInformation and panel interfaces, so replay saves only the Application/Page/Timer/InputPane/HardwareButtons plumbing.

FL 9_1: CreateDeviceResources requests {11_1,11_0,10_1,10_0,9_3} with Flags=0. The clamp is mandatory on Surface RT. Also the swap chain is created with IDXGIFactory2::CreateSwapChainForComposition and then IDXGISwapChain2::SetMatrixTransform is invoked (slot 34): provide a composition-capable swap chain (DirectComposition target on the HWND) or intercept both.

Keyboard (TabTip) contract: the game never calls the Win32 touch keyboard; it focuses the XAML TextBox 'EditBox' (HID lambdas, TextBox2.PreventKeyboardDisplayOnProgrammaticFocus) and focuses the Button to dismiss, and learns the keyboard height ONLY through InputPane Showing/Hiding events -> AppMain::onKeyboardHeightChanged(px). A host fake should map EditBox focus/unfocus to show/hide of TabTip and raise InputPane Hiding/Showing (get_OccludedRect height) deterministically from its own state machine instead of relying on TabTip window events.
